clue.text: The citadel's harvest stored in a specially-built silo

indicators.note: the harvest word is put away inside the other letters, as grain goes into a silo
something specially built is constructed anew, so the letters of silo are rearranged

parts.note: a harvest is a crop

explanation.surface: Grain from the fortress is kept in a purpose-built silo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The citadel's' gives the definition with a link 's (is); 'harvest' hides the grain inside the anagram of the silo letters, as the surface stores grain in a silo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the ancient hilltop fortress of Athens, and the word means a Greek city's citadel generally.

clue.text: Most friendly when drink is provided

definitions.text: Most friendly when drink is provided

parts.words: Most friendly when drink is provided
parts.note: a word meaning warm and friendly is also the name of a sweet fruit drink, so hospitality comes with a glass

explanation.surface: People are at their warmest once the drinks come out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means warmly friendly and also a concentrated fruit drink or liqueur.

clue.text: Out-of-the-ordinary but unsatisfactory buffet

parts.note: food or a performance that is off is not up to standard
to buffet is to beat or strike repeatedly

explanation.surface: An unusual, disappointing spread of food at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal but is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconventional or quirky is described as off the beaten track, unusual.

clue.text: Striking the Conservatives as comprehensive

parts.note: workers on strike are said to be out
the Conservatives are the political right

explanation.surface: A strike by the Tories proves to be total.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete, total victory is an unqualified one, with no reservation.

clue.text: Animals bringing food to a holy man

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
oats are food, for horses or as porridge

explanation.surface: Creatures carry provisions to a saintly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats are small carnivorous mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: Created a row about egghead woman

parts.note: made means created

indicators.note: the row word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a line is a row
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual woman is the cause of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual describing the woman, but it is just the head (first letter) of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleine is a girl's name, a woman's.

clue.text: Support to finish with gold points

parts.note: an end is a finish
or is the heraldic word for gold
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Backing a team to end up with gold medals.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to back or approve it.

clue.text: Making decrees at discovering misuse

indicators.note: making the letters into something new signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Issuing orders on finding something abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovering' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate is to treat something sacred with violent disrespect, an abuse of it.

clue.text: There's a fall in support for a golfer under instruction

definitions.note: describes the person being taught, a noun's sense given adjectivally

indicators.note: the fall word sits inside the golfer's support

parts.note: a tee holds up a golf ball, the golfer's support
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A golfer having a lesson sees a downpour on the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests stumbling, but it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in training is one receiving instruction.

clue.text: Collieries holding back on account of yields

indicators.note: the collieries word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: coal mines are pits

indicators.note: the word for 'on account of' is read backwards

parts.note: for means because of, on account of

explanation.surface: Coal mines keep back money from their returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Profits are returns on investment, what a business brings in.

clue.text: Bloomer made by singularly mean individual

indicators.note: the letters of mean are made into something new, an anagram

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a uniquely stingy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower; 'singularly' only stresses one.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemone is a flowering plant, so a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Spot fruit that's underweight

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
light means weighing too little

explanation.surface: Picking out a piece of fruit that weighs too little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb but is a spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public glare, like a stage spotlight.

clue.text: Hang around an old German city

indicators.note: the hang word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to hover is to hang in the air

explanation.surface: Loitering about a historic town in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is a city in Lower Saxony, once capital of a kingdom.

clue.text: He takes the measure of fools, endlessly kind

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: the kind word loses its last letter

parts.note: a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: A man who sizes up idiots, without end of kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates value or tax, gauging how much something is worth.

clue.text: Grab litter

definitions.meaning: a set of eggs or young hatched together

explanation.definitionFit: To clutch is to seize; a clutch is a brood of eggs or chicks.

clue.text: She doesn't expect to succeed all on her own

definitions.text: She doesn't expect to succeed all on her own

parts.words: She doesn't expect to succeed all on her own
parts.note: succeed means inherit: a woman who shares an inheritance with others

explanation.surface: A woman lacking confidence that she can manage alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who inherits jointly with others.

clue.text: Anti-hunt meeting

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to course is to hunt hares with hounds

explanation.surface: A gathering of protesters against blood sports.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a crowd gathered together, an assembly.

clue.text: The turk to turn to (male)

indicators.note: the first 'to' is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A Turkish man one can call on for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' acts only on the first 'to'; the second stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ottoman is a subject of the old Turkish empire.

clue.text: Converts so gained were not happy

definitions.note: a past verb, matching the past-tense answer

indicators.note: converting the letters turns them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: New believers won over in this way were miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agonised is to have suffered anguish or worried hard.

clue.text: Felt in some discomfort again and stretched

parts.note: re- means again
ached means hurt mildly

explanation.surface: Sore once more after a good stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reached is to have extended or stretched out a hand.

clue.text: He's written stuff about the Orient

indicators.note: the stuff word goes round the other letter

parts.note: to gorge is to stuff oneself
E is east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A man who writes material concerning the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on George Eliot and George Sand, women who wrote under a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a man's name, also the pen name of women novelists Eliot and Sand.

clue.text: Work with favoured unit on view

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
in means popular, favoured
I is one, a unit

explanation.surface: Working with a preferred piece in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a personal view or belief.

clue.text: Engendering grace in a European

indicators.note: engendering means producing something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing out elegance in someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grecian is a Greek, a native of a European country.

clue.text: Training cut out without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the cut word wraps the other

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Practice was dropped without any pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical training or practice.

clue.text: Position — give voice about it

indicators.note: the singing word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to sing is to give voice

explanation.surface: Where to stand to sing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting is placing something, giving it a position.

clue.text: He's not digging up material for the press!

definitions.text: He's not digging up material for the press!

parts.words: He's not digging up material for the press!
parts.note: not a journalist hunting stories: he extracts the metal used for pressing clothes

explanation.surface: A man who is no investigative reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who mines iron ore.

clue.text: Tell military personnel to accompany a noble foreigner

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a count is a European nobleman, not a British title

explanation.surface: Ask soldiers to escort an aristocrat from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate or tell it.

clue.text: In Paris questionable pharmacies supply it

indicators.note: questionable means doubtful, so the letters are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dodgy chemist shops in Paris sell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller sold by chemists.

clue.text: The Texan's topping!

parts.note: topping means a hat, not something superb: what a Texan wears on his head

explanation.surface: A man from Texas is splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the broad-brimmed cowboy hat.

clue.text: Leisure activity of a down-to earth stay-at-home

definitions.text: Leisure activity of a down-to earth stay-at-home

parts.words: Leisure activity of a down-to earth stay-at-home
parts.note: down-to-earth taken literally: a hobby working the soil around one's own home

explanation.surface: The pastime of a practical homebody.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardening is the hobby of tending plants and soil.
